q: Why is a control tube containing glass beads of the same volume as the seeds set up beside the respirometer?
options: To correct for gas volume changes caused by temperature or pressure, not by respiration
To supply extra oxygen to the seeds in the experimental tube as their supply runs low
To absorb the carbon dioxide produced by the seeds in the experimental tube
To make sure the seeds in the experimental tube receive exactly the same light intensity
explanation: Gas volume changes with temperature and atmospheric pressure. A tube with non-living material of equal volume experiences the same physical changes, so any movement there can be subtracted (or the two tubes can be connected as a differential respirometer). Keeping the apparatus in a thermostatically controlled water bath also reduces this error.
